Its fortified granaries, ancient mosques and silent alleys tell the story of a caravan crossroads now asleep.

L'Empire du Mali absorbe les territoires: The Mali Empire absorbs the Sahelian territories of present-day Mauritania. The cities of Timbuktu and Djenné become intellectual and commercial crossroads. The gold of Bambouk and Bouré makes the empire famous throughout the Mediterranean world.
L'accueil des Mauritaniens est chaleureu: The Mauritanian welcome is warm. Mint tea is an experience in itself.
L'addax est un mammifère emblématique du: The addax is an iconic mammal of the Mauritanian Sahara. With its spiral horns and a coat that changes from white in winter to grey in summer, it can survive several months without water. Unfortunately, heavily hunted, the species is now critically endangered with fewer than 100 individuals in the wild. The Banc d'Arguin Park and the protected areas of Adrar are its last refuges.
L'agriculture et l'élevage occupent une: Agriculture and livestock farming hold an important place in the traditional economy. The cultivation of millet, sorghum and dates, as well as cattle, sheep and camel rearing, sustain the livelihoods of a large part of the rural population. The services and telecommunications sector is booming, driven by digitalisation and infrastructure development.
L'ardin est une petite harpe à 7 cordes: The ardin is a small 7-string harp played exclusively by women. This delicate instrument produces soft, contemplative melodies. It is associated with intimate moments — lullabies, love songs, hair-dressing ceremonies. The ardin is a symbol of femininity and elegance in Moorish culture.
L'art de la calligraphie arabe est très: The art of Arabic calligraphy is widely practised, notably for decorating mosques and Quranic schools. The manuscripts of Chinguetti bear witness to this tradition.
L'artisanat mauritanien est le reflet d': Mauritanian crafts reflect a thousand-year-old cultural heritage: Moorish tapestries, silver jewellery, pottery and nomadic objects — every piece tells a story.
L'aéroport international de Nouakchott-O: Nouakchott-Oumtounsy International Airport (NKC) is the country's main hub, with connections to Paris, Casablanca, Istanbul and Dubai. Nouadhibou Airport (NDB) serves regional routes and domestic flights. Atar Airport (ATR) serves Adrar and the northern tourist circuits.
L'hassaniya est un dialecte arabe distin: Hassaniya is a distinct Arabic dialect, enriched by borrowings from Berber and African languages. It is the language of poetry, tales and proverbs. Moorish griots cultivate it in epic recitations that keep tribal memory alive. Hassaniya is characterised by guttural sounds and a singing melody that sets it apart from other Arabic dialects.
L'hymne national et les grandes voix de: The national anthem and the great voices of Mauritanian music.
L'instrument emblématique des Maures, un: The iconic instrument of the Moors, a plucked-string zither made of wood and goatskin.
L'islam sunnite de rite malékite est la: Sunni Islam of the Maliki rite is the religion of the entire population. Sufi brotherhoods, marabouts and Quranic schools structure spiritual and social life.
L'islam sunnite de rite malékite s'impla: Sunni Islam of the Maliki rite gradually established itself through trade and the influence of Arab tribes from the north. The first mosques were built in caravan cities such as Chinguetti and Ouadane, which became major religious and intellectual centres in West Africa.
L'oasis de Terjit est un véritable havre: The oasis of Terjit is a real haven of peace nestled in a narrow gorge in the heart of Adrar. Its palm trees, natural hot springs and small waterfalls make it a swimming and relaxation spot much loved by travellers. After a day in the desert, nothing beats a dip in the warm waters of Terjit to recharge.
L'urbanisation est passée de 5% en 1960: Urbanisation rose from 5% in 1960 to 62% in 2024. Nouakchott, which was a small village at independence, now concentrates nearly a third of the national population. This rapid growth reflects rural exodus and economic centralisation.
L'écart d'alphabétisation entre hommes e: The literacy gap between men and women remains worrying. Government efforts focus on adult literacy programmes, modernised Quranic schools and girls' education in rural areas.
L'école coranique (mahadra) est la premi: The Quranic school (mahadra) is the first school in the life of a Mauritanian child. Children begin learning the Quran from the age of 4-5, by heart and in recitation. Quranic masters (moualim) are respected and 'khattam' ceremonies (completing the reading of the Quran) are important family events.
L'économie mauritanienne repose principa: The Mauritanian economy relies mainly on mining, which accounts for about 35% of GDP. Iron ore, mined at Zouérate, is the country's top resource. Mauritania has also become a significant producer of gold and copper, attracting substantial foreign investment.
L'éducation coranique est la base histor: Quranic education is the historical foundation of teaching in Mauritania. Quranic schools ('mahadras') trained generations of scholars in the holy cities of Chinguetti, Ouadane, Tichitt and Oualata. Quranic masters ('moualim') teach Quran reading, Arabic grammar, Islamic law and logic. Today, the modern education system seeks to integrate the best practices of Quranic teaching into the national curriculum.
L'éducation en Mauritanie est en pleine: Education in Mauritania is undergoing a major transformation, between the heritage of Quranic schools and the modernisation of the school system.
L'élection de Mohamed Ould Cheikh El Gha: The election of Mohamed Ould Cheikh El Ghazouani marks the first peaceful transition between two elected presidents since independence.
L'Œil du Sahara ou structure de Richat e: The Eye of the Sahara or Richat Structure is a one-of-a-kind geological formation. This concentric circle 50 km in diameter, visible from space, has intrigued scientists for decades. Long thought to be a meteorite impact crater, it is in fact a geological dome eroded by wind and water. The site offers spectacular views from the surrounding cliffs.
La Constitution du 20 juillet 1991 intro: The Constitution of 20 July 1991 introduces multi-party politics and structures the regime around the presidency, the government and parliament.
La Constitution du 20 juillet 1991 régit: The Constitution of 20 July 1991 governs the Mauritanian State.
La Cour suprême est la plus haute juridi: The Supreme Court is the highest jurisdiction. Sharia is a source of law, and Islamic courts handle personal matters.
La France établit un protectorat sur la: France establishes a protectorate over Mauritania as part of its conquest of French West Africa. The emirates are gradually subdued by force, notably after the battle of Tijigja. Governor Coppolani plays a key role in pacifying the territory.
La Mauritanie a adopté une politique d'é: Mauritania has adopted a nomadic education policy for herders' children, with mobile schools and distance-learning programmes. The challenge remains ensuring continuity of schooling across such a vast geographical landscape.
La Mauritanie annexe le tiers sud du Sah: Mauritania annexes the southern third of Western Sahara after the departure of the Spanish, but must face the Polisario Front guerrilla. Attacks on the mining infrastructure of Zouérate weaken the economy. In 1978, a military coup ends the presidency of Ould Daddah and Mauritania abandons its territorial claims.
La Mauritanie compte environ 4,6 million: Mauritania has about 4.6 million inhabitants. Its population is young and mostly urban, with a rich ethnic diversity reflecting its history as a crossroads between North Africa and sub-Saharan Africa.
La Mauritanie devient une colonie frança: Mauritania becomes a French colony within French West Africa.
La Mauritanie est officiellement intégré: Mauritania is officially integrated into AOF (French West Africa) as a distinct colony. Saint-Louis du Sénégal serves as the administrative capital. The colonial administration imposes new taxes, recruits Senegalese riflemen and develops an extractive economy centred on iron and salt.
La Mauritanie est un carrefour de civili: Mauritania is a crossroads of civilisations. Land of the Almoravids who shaped the history of North Africa and Al-Andalus, it has seen empires, emirates and colonisation follow one another. Since its independence in 1960, it has built a modern nation while preserving its ancestral traditions.
La Mauritanie est un carrefour linguisti: Mauritania is a unique linguistic crossroads where Hassaniya Arabic, French, Pulaar, Soninké and Wolof coexist — each carrying a specific cultural richness.
La Mauritanie est une république islamiq: Mauritania is an Islamic republic whose political system is based on the Constitution of 20 July 1991. The President of the Republic, elected by direct universal suffrage for a five-year term renewable once, is the Head of State and holds extensive executive powers. He appoints the Prime Minister and the government.
Mauritania is a semi-presidential Islamic republic.
Mauritania is a semi-presidential Islamic republic. The president shares executive power with the Prime Minister and the government.
La Mauritanie proclame son indépendance: Mauritania proclaims its independence on 28 November 1960.
Mauritania proclaims its independence on 28 November 1960. Mokhtar Ould Daddah becomes the first president and lays the foundations of national institutions.
La République Islamique de Mauritanie es: The Islamic Republic of Mauritania is a semi-presidential state where the president and parliament share executive and legislative power.
La bijouterie mauritanienne, héritière d: Mauritanian jewellery, heir to Berber and Moorish traditions, is renowned for its solid silver pieces. Necklaces, bracelets and rings are adorned with yellow amber ('karf'), red coral and semi-precious stones. Moorish women wear these jewels at ceremonies and weddings, and they are an essential part of the traditional dowry.
La cuisine mauritanienne est un métissag: Mauritanian cuisine is a blend of African, Arab and Berber flavours. Between sauce dishes, honey pastries and the famous mint tea, it tells the story of a proud and hospitable people.
La cérémonie du thé en Mauritanie est bi: The tea ceremony in Mauritania is much more than a simple preparation. It is an essential social ritual that symbolises hospitality and friendship. Mint tea is prepared in a traditional teapot and served in three successive glasses: the first is strong like death, the second is sweet like life, the third is fragrant like love. Each glass is shared among guests, creating moments of conviviality and exchange.
La danse traditionnelle avec les épées (: The traditional sword dance ('raïcha') is performed at festivals and ceremonies, a symbol of bravery and warrior tradition.
La discipline la plus traditional de Mau: The most traditional discipline in Mauritania.
La faune mauritanienne, mélange unique d: Mauritanian fauna, a unique mix of Saharan and Sahelian species.
La gerboise du Sahara est un petit mammi: The Sahara jerboa is a small jumping mammal that lives in the sandy dunes of Mauritania. With its long hind legs and ability to dig deep burrows, it survives the scorching daytime heat and the desert's cold nights. It feeds on seeds, insects and the dew it collects from plants at dawn. Its sandy coat makes it almost invisible in the desert landscape.
La harpe des femmes maures, joué lors de: The harp of Moorish women, played at ceremonies and festivals.
La lutte maure est un sport ancestral qu: Moorish wrestling is an ancestral sport practised at festivals and ceremonies.
La lutte traditionnelle est un sport pro: Traditional wrestling is a sport deeply rooted in Mauritanian culture. Fights ('tahta') take place on sand, without strict rules, and the fighters wear leather shorts. Wrestling tournaments are major social events, accompanied by music, songs and feasts. Wrestling champions are highly respected local heroes.
La lutte traditionnelle mauritanienne es: Traditional Mauritanian wrestling is much more than a sport: it is a social ritual that perpetuates the values of bravery, honour and respect. Fights take place on a sand ring, with no time limit, until a wrestler is pinned to the ground. Wrestling champions are revered figures in society, and tournaments attract thousands of spectators. The 'maâlems' (wrestling masters) have passed on their knowledge from father to son for generations.
La musique mauritanienne est un univers: Mauritanian music is a world of vibrant strings, powerful percussion and ancestral songs, carried by the oral tradition of the griots.
La nuit ne brille pas et demain ne brill: The night does not shine and tomorrow does not shine
La patience est la mère de toutes les ve: Patience is the mother of all virtues.
La plus grande tortue marine au monde, n: The largest sea turtle in the world, nesting on the beaches of the Mauritanian coast.
La population mauritanienne est passée d: The Mauritanian population grew from 854,000 in 1960 to 4.62 million in 2024, a 5.4-fold increase in 64 years. Population growth remains strong with a fertility rate of 4.5 children per woman.
La poterie mauritanienne se distingue pa: Mauritanian pottery stands out for its rustic quality and functional shapes. The potters of the southern regions — Gorgol, Guidimaka, Brakna — use techniques passed down from mother to daughter. Water canaries ('darba'), millet jars and cooking pots are decorated with incised and painted geometric patterns.
La pêche est le deuxième pilier économiq: Fishing is the second economic pillar. With 754 km of coastline among the richest in fish in Africa, this sector employs tens of thousands of people. Mauritanian waters attract international fishing fleets, and Nouadhibou is the main processing and export centre for fishery products.
La richesse culturelle se transmet de bo: Cultural richness has been passed down by word of mouth for centuries.
La région est intégrée à l'Empire du Mal: The region is integrated into the Mali Empire under Soundiata Keïta.
La réélection du président Ghazouani con: President Ghazouani's re-election confirms the continuity of the semi-presidential regime and the stability of contemporary institutions.
La sagesse du peuple mauritanien en quel: The wisdom of the Mauritanian people in a few words.
La sagesse mauritanienne s'exprime à tra: Mauritanian wisdom is expressed through striking proverbs that guide social behaviour and interpersonal relations.
La tortue luth, pouvant atteindre 2 mètr: The leatherback turtle, reaching up to 2 metres long and weighing 900 kg, frequents Mauritanian waters to feed on jellyfish. Females come to lay their eggs on the coast's beaches, notably in the Banc d'Arguin region. The beaches of Lévrier and Port Étienne are important nesting sites. Threats include accidental fishing, egg poaching and the loss of their coastal habitat.
La tradition poétique hassaniya est l'un: The Hassaniya poetic tradition is one of the pillars of Mauritanian culture. Poets ('sha'er') play a crucial social role, resolving conflicts, celebrating unions and preserving tribal history.
La vannerie est un artisanat omniprésent: Basketry is an omnipresent craft in Mauritania, particularly in the oases of Adrar and the Sahelian zones. Date-palm, esparto and reed fibres are turned into baskets ('ghaba'), mats, hats and birdcages. The weaving technique varies by region, creating distinctive patterns.
La vie végétale s'adapte aux conditions: Plant life adapts to the extreme conditions of the Sahara.
Lait fermenté traditionnel, boisson rafr: Traditional fermented milk, a refreshing and nutritious drink.
Langue mandingue du sud-ouest, partagée: A Mande language of the south-west, shared with neighbouring Senegal.
Langue mandingue parlée dans le sud, ass: A Mande language spoken in the south, associated with the medieval Ghana civilisation.
Langue peule parlée dans le sud et le su: A Fulani language spoken in the south and south-east, rich in pastoral and poetic vocabulary.
Langues culture arabe français pulaar so: Languages culture Arabic French Pulaar Soninke Wolof oral traditions
Langues, traditions orales et proverbes: Mauritanian languages, oral traditions and proverbs
Le 22 juin 2019, Mohamed Ould Cheikh El: On 22 June 2019, Mohamed Ould Cheikh El Ghazouani, a former Defence Minister, wins the presidential election. It is the first peaceful and democratic change of power since independence. The poll is judged broadly transparent by international observers, marking progress for Mauritanian democracy.
Le 28 novembre 1960, la République Islam: On 28 November 1960, the Islamic Republic of Mauritania proclaims its independence with Mokhtar Ould Daddah as first president. The country adopts a constitution and joins the UN and the Arab League. Nouakchott, then a small village, is chosen as capital and grows rapidly.
Le Grand Marché de Nouakchott est le cœu: The Grand Marché of Nouakchott is the beating heart of Mauritanian crafts. Its narrow alleys are full of silver jewellery, hand-woven rugs, colourful pottery and fragrant leathers. Artisans come from all over the country to sell their creations. In Nouadhibou, the fish market is accompanied by a craft district specialising in leatherwork and jewellery. In Adrar, the oases of Chinguetti and Atar host craft fairs where Moorish rugs and carved wooden objects reign.
Le PIB mauritanien est passé de 5,8 à 10: Mauritania's GDP rose from $5.8 to $10.4 billion between 2015 and 2024, an average growth of 6.7% per year. This progress is driven by the mining boom (iron, gold, copper) and rising investment in infrastructure.
Le Parc National du Banc d'Arguin est l': The Banc d'Arguin National Park is one of the world's most important bird sanctuaries. A UNESCO World Heritage site since 1989, it spans over 12,000 km² between desert and ocean. The shallow waters of its lagoons shelter millions of migratory birds — flamingos, pelicans, terns and herons. The Imraguen fishermen, a traditional community, practise environmentally-friendly artisanal fishing there.

The Banc d'Arguin National Park is one of Africa's most important ornithological sites. A UNESCO World Heritage site since 1989, it welcomes over 2 million migratory birds from Europe and Asia every year. The shallow lagoon waters, rich in fish and invertebrates, offer an unmatched feast for flamingos, pelicans, terns, herons and many other species.
Le Parc du Banc d'Arguin est un paradis: The Banc d'Arguin Park is a paradise for birdwatchers. Magnificent!
Le Parlement vote les lois et contrôle l: Parliament votes on laws and controls the government. It is made up of the National Assembly (157 deputies) and the Senate. The last legislative election took place in 2023.
Le Ramadan est la période la plus intens: Ramadan is the most intense period of the religious year in Mauritania. Mosques organise 'tarawih' (night prayers) and iftars (fast-breaking meals) for the faithful. Markets come alive in the evening, and families gather to break the fast together. Ramadan is also a time of charity and solidarity.
Le Train des Sables est l'un des trains: The Iron Ore Train is one of Africa's most iconic trains. 2.5 km long, it crosses the desert between the Zouérate iron mine and the port of Nouadhibou over 704 km. It carries iron ore but also transports passengers on the stretch between Nouadhibou and Zouérate. The journey lasts about 12 hours and offers a unique spectacle: hundreds of open wagons crossing the Sahara.
Le Train des Sables est l'un des voyages: The Iron Ore Train is one of the most spectacular journeys in the world. 2.5 kilometres long, it has carried iron ore from the Zouérate mine to the port of Nouadhibou since 1963. Bold travellers climb aboard the open wagons, sitting on bags of ore, for a 12 to 17-hour journey across the Sahara. The sight of golden dunes at sunset from an ore wagon is unforgettable. This train is also the longest rail convoy in the world.
Le Train des Sables, longest train du mo: The Iron Ore Train, the longest train in the world, connects Zouérate to the port of Nouadhibou.
Le bois est une ressource rare en Maurit: Wood is a rare resource in Mauritania, which makes carving all the more precious. Artisans mainly work with tamarisk, acacia and jujube to create everyday objects: millet pestles, dough boards, stools and chests. The carved patterns echo the geometric symbols found in tapestry and architecture.
Le calendrier religieux rythme la vie ma: The religious calendar shapes Mauritanian life. Eid al-Fitr marks the end of Ramadan with collective prayers and feasts. Eid al-Adha (Tabaski) commemorates Abraham's sacrifice with the slaughtering of a sheep. Mawlid celebrates the birth of the Prophet with religious songs and processions.
Le chameau reste le moyen de transport t: The camel remains the traditional means of transport for nomads in the deep desert.
Le chant religieux soufi, avec ses« dhik: Sufi religious chanting, with its 'dhikr' and 'madih', holds an important place in Mauritanian spiritual life.
Le cheval ne se laisse monter que par ce: A horse only lets itself be ridden by one who knows it
Le cuir est une matière première essenti: Leather is an essential raw material of nomadic crafts. Moorish backpacks ('tara'), leather sandals and dromedary bridles are crafted with simple tools but great skill. Tanning uses natural tannins from acacia bark. The cut-outs and incisions create geometric patterns that identify tribal origin.
Le cyclisme gagne en popularité, avec de: Cycling is gaining in popularity, with races through the desert and the Sahara tracks.
Le cyclisme s'est développé ces dernière: Cycling has developed in recent years, driven by the challenges of the desert terrain. Races like the 'Tour de Mauritanie' cover hundreds of kilometres across the country's roads and tracks. Cycling is also a cheap means of transport in the cities, especially for delivery riders.
Le dromadaire est au cœur de la civilisa: The dromedary has been at the heart of the Mauritanian nomadic civilisation for millennia. It provides milk, meat, leather and wool, and carries goods across the desert. The Mauritanian herd numbers about 1.5 million head. Moorish nomadic herders share a deep spiritual and cultural bond with these animals, which play a central role in marriages, ceremonies and social organisation.
Le dromadaire est le moyen de transport: The dromedary is the oldest means of transport and the best adapted to the extreme conditions of the Sahara. Moorish nomads use it for daily travel, transporting goods and seasonal migration. A dromedary can cover 40 km a day carrying up to 200 kg. Camel races ('fantasia') are a very popular traditional sport.
Le faucon pèlerin est un visiteur réguli: The peregrine falcon is a regular visitor to Mauritania, particularly along the Atlantic coast and in the coastal areas of Banc d'Arguin. With dives reaching 390 km/h, it is the fastest animal on the planet. Migratory populations pass through Mauritania during the season changes, taking advantage of the concentrations of migrants along the coastline.
Le fondement historique de l'apprentissa: The historical foundation of learning in Mauritania.
Le football est de loin le sport le plus: Football is by far the most played and followed sport in Mauritania. The national championship (Ligue 1) has 14 teams including FC Nouadhibou, ASC Mauritanie and FC de l'Avenir. The national team, nicknamed 'The Mourabitounes', made its Africa Cup of Nations debut in 2019. The municipal stadiums of Nouakchott and Nouadhibou are hotbeds of energy at the weekend.
Le français est la langue dominante de l: French is the dominant language of administration, justice and higher education. It coexists with Arabic in all official documents. The written press, television and the business world use French widely, although a gradual Arabisation policy has been under way since the 1990s.
Le galago ou tama est un petit tambour d: The galago or tama is a small drum whose membrane is tightened by crossed cords on the sides. By pressing these cords against his chest while playing, the musician can change the tension of the skin and thus produce spectacular tonal variations. This instrument is used in faster, more danceable rhythms, notably at naming ceremonies and festivals.
Le grand tambour cérémoniel, battu lors: The great ceremonial drum, beaten at weddings, births and religious festivals.
Le général Mohamed Ould Abdel Aziz renve: General Mohamed Ould Abdel Aziz overthrows elected president Sidi Ould Cheikh Abdallahi. The putsch is condemned by the international community, but Ould Abdel Aziz wins the 2009 presidential election. His term is marked by relative stability and economic growth driven by mining and oil.
Le handball est en pleine croissance en: Handball is growing fast in Mauritania, especially in urban centres. The national league includes men's and women's teams. Handball is played in schools and sports centres, and the national team takes part in regional competitions in West Africa.
Le minerai de fer représente 42% des exp: Iron ore accounts for 42% of total exports, making Mauritania one of Africa's main exporters. Gold (18%) and fishery products (16%) are the second and third items, while copper and hydrocarbons complete the export basket.
Le mois sacré est vécu avec une ferveur: The holy month is lived with particular fervour, with night prayers and collective iftars.
Le mortier à grains transformé en instru: The grain mortar turned into a musical instrument by women.
Le motif a été répété pour créer un effe: The pattern has been repeated to create a weaving effect.
Le parlement bicaméral comprend l'Assemb: The bicameral parliament comprises the National Assembly (157 deputies) and the Senate. It votes on laws and controls the government's action.
Le parlement est bicaméral, composé de l: Parliament is bicameral, made up of the National Assembly (157 deputies elected for 5 years) and the Senate (abolished in 2017 then restored). The judiciary is independent, with the Supreme Court as the highest jurisdiction. Islam is the state religion, and sharia is a source of law.
Le pays est divisé en 15 wilayas (région: The country is divided into 15 wilayas (regions), each with its own characteristics.
Le pays est découpé en 15 wilayas (régio: The country is divided into 15 wilayas (regions).
Le phoque moine du Sahara est une espèce: The Saharan monk seal is a species endemic to the Mauritanian coast. With about 400 individuals left, it is the rarest seal in the world. It lives mainly in the Baie du Lévrier and on the rocks of Cap Blanc. Its population was decimated by hunting and accidental fishing, but recent conservation efforts have slowed the decline.
Le port de Nouakchott, inauguré en 1986,: The port of Nouakchott, opened in 1986, is the country's main port with a handling capacity of 2 million tonnes a year. The older port of Nouadhibou is the largest fishing port in West Africa. Maritime transport handles most foreign trade, imports and ore exports.
Le président de la République, élu au su: The President of the Republic, elected by direct universal suffrage for 5 years, shares executive power with the Prime Minister and the government. The regime combines features of the presidential system — an elected head of state with extensive powers — and of the parliamentary system, with a government accountable to the National Assembly.
Le président est le chef de l'État. Il n: The president is the Head of State. He appoints the Prime Minister and the government. The presidential term is 5 years, renewable once.
Le président est élu au suffrage univers: The president is elected by direct universal suffrage for a 5-year term, renewable only once since the constitutional reform.
Le président sortant Mohamed Ould Cheikh: Outgoing president Mohamed Ould Cheikh El Ghazouani is re-elected in the first round of the June 2024 presidential election. The poll confirms the country's political stability in a tense regional context. The new term focuses on economic diversification, regional security and infrastructure development.
Le pulaar est la langue des Peuls (Fulbé: Pulaar is the language of the Fulani (Fulbé), herders and pastoralists spread across West Africa. In Mauritania it is mainly spoken in the regions of Brakna, Gorgol, Guidimaka and Hodh El Gharbi. Pulaar has a rich vocabulary for describing herds, seasons and social relations. It is also the language of Pulaaku, the Fulani code of honour.
Le rapace le plus rapide du monde, fréqu: The fastest bird of prey in the world, frequently seen along the Mauritanian coast.
Le réseau routier mauritanien comprend e: Mauritania's road network totals about 7,700 km, of which only 3,100 km are paved. The main national roads link Nouakchott to Nouadhibou (N1), Nouakchott to Rosso (N3) and Nouakchott to Néma (N7). Dirt tracks connect the villages and oases of the interior. The rainy season (July to September) makes many tracks impassable.
Le réseau routier relie les grandes vill: The road network links the big cities, but desert tracks remain predominant.
Le secteur minier domine avec 35% du PIB: The mining sector dominates with 35% of GDP, thanks to the iron deposits of Zouérate and the gold mines of Tasiast. Fishing (20%) and services (18%) complete the economic fabric. Agriculture, though a minority in value, employs a large share of the rural population.
Le seul mammifère marin endémique d'Afri: Africa's only endemic marine mammal, living in the waters of the Baie du Lévrier.
Le son de la Mauritanie se joue sur des: The sound of Mauritania is played on ancestral instruments.
Le soninké est la langue des Soninkés, d: Soninké is the language of the Soninke, descendants of the ancient Ghana Empire. It is spoken in the regions of Hodh Ech Chargui, Guidimaka and Assaba. This Mande language has a complex tonal system and a rich repertoire of historical narratives that keep alive the memory of the Wagadou (Ghana) empire.
Le sport le plus populaire du pays. La L: The most popular sport in the country. The Mauritanian Ligue 1 has 14 teams and the national team took part in AFCON 2019.
Le tambour à cordes croisées, dont la te: The drum with crossed cords, whose tension varies to change the tone while playing.
Le taux d'alphabétisation de 52% cache d: The 52% literacy rate hides strong disparities: 69% among men versus 36% among women, and 67% in urban areas versus 33% in rural areas.
Le tbal est un grand tambour à membrane: The tbal is a large single-membrane drum, made from a hollowed tree trunk and a stretched goatskin. It is the most used instrument at traditional ceremonies. The rhythm of the tbal is hypnotic and powerful, capable of carrying collective dances for hours. Professional tbal players are essential figures of social life.
Le tendé est un grand mortier en bois tr: The tendé is a large wooden mortar traditionally used to pound millet. During the 'tendé' ceremonies (a name that comes from the mortar itself), women sing and beat the rhythm on the mortar walls with wooden pestles. This tradition is at the origin of many popular Mauritanian songs and is a highlight of community life.
Le tidinit est le précurseur de la guita: The tidinit is the forerunner of the African guitar. This plucked-string instrument, made of tamarisk wood and goatskin, accompanies Moorish griots in their poetic and epic recitations. It usually has between 4 and 6 strings and produces a soft, melancholic sound. The greatest tidinit players are considered national treasures.
Le tir à l'arc traditionnel est pratiqué: Traditional archery is practised mainly by the Fulani and Soninke communities of the south. The wooden bows are handcrafted and competitions take place during agrarian festivals. This sport requires great precision and exceptional concentration. Tournaments are accompanied by traditional dances and songs.
Le tissage des tapis est une tradition e: Rug weaving is an exclusively female tradition in Mauritania. 'Hanib' weavings use the wool of local goats and sheep, dyed with natural pigments. The patterns — diamonds, zigzags, crossed diamonds — carry symbolic meanings linked to protection, fertility and tribal identity. A single rug can take months of work.
Le wolof est parlé par la communauté wol: Wolof is spoken by Mauritania's Wolof community, concentrated in the Trarza region and Nouakchott. Though a minority in the country, it is the most spoken language in Senegal, creating cross-border cultural ties. Wolof is a dynamic language that borrows easily from other languages.
Les Haratines (Maures noirs) forment le: The Haratines (black Moors) form the largest group with 40% of the population, followed by the Beidanes (white Moors) with 30%. The Fulani (15%), Soninke (8%), Wolof (5%) and Bambara (2%) complete the country's ethnic mosaic.
Les appels à la prière (adhan) résonnent: The calls to prayer (adhan) echo five times a day in all the country's towns and villages. Mosques are always full, especially for Friday prayer (salat al-jumua). Shops close during prayer times, and social life is organised around these sacred moments.
Les artisans de Nouakchott et de Chingue: The artisans of Nouakchott and Chinguetti create chiselled silver pieces adorned with amber and coral.
Les chefs d'État de la Mauritanie depuis: The heads of state of Mauritania since independence.
Les chefs religieux (« marabouts ») joue: Religious leaders ('marabouts') play a considerable social and spiritual role.
Les contes transmis de génération en gén: Tales handed down from generation to generation tell of the exploits of ancestors, the secrets of caravans and the lessons of nomadic life. The storyteller ('maâlem') is a respected figure.
Les courses de chameaux sont un spectacl: Camel races are a unique spectacle in the Sahara, with significant financial stakes.
Les courses de dromadaires sont le sport: Camel racing is the equestrian sport of the Sahara. The animals, often fitted with cameras and GPS, cover distances of 20 to 50 km in the dunes. Camel owners compete for prizes that can reach millions of ouguiyas. Races mainly take place in winter, during the cultural festivals of Adrar and Tagant.
Les dimensions sociales et spirituelles: The social and spiritual dimensions of music.
Les femmes jouent un rôle fondamental da: Women play a fundamental role in Mauritanian music. Female artists, notably the 'layalat' (singers), are the guardians of the female oral tradition. They sing at weddings, births and hair-dressing ceremonies. Contemporary singers such as Dimi Mint Abba and Malouma Mattala have carried Mauritanian music onto the international stage, blending ancient traditions with modern influences. The ardin, played exclusively by women, is the symbol of this female musical tradition.
Les fouilles archéologiques dans l'Adrar: Archaeological excavations in Adrar and Tagant have revealed stone tools, rock paintings and burials dating from the Neolithic. The Sahara was then a green savannah populated by hunter-gatherers and early herders. Rock engravings of animals now extinct bear witness to this era when the climate was much wetter.

Les griots (« maâlem ») sont les déposit: Griots ('maâlem') are the keepers of oral memory. They sing of the exploits of ancestors, tribal lineages and historical events at official and private ceremonies.
Les marabouts sont les guides spirituels: Marabouts are the spiritual guides of Mauritanian society. They lead Sufi brotherhoods, teach the Quran and advise families. The great maraboutic families (Idaw Ali, Idaw M-Barek, Tijaani) have considerable social influence. The faithful come from all over the country to seek the advice and blessings of respected marabouts.
Les mariages mauritaniens sont accompagn: Mauritanian weddings are accompanied by specific songs: dowry songs ('sdaq'), songs of joy and wedding lullabies.

Les principales institutions sont la Pré: The main institutions are the Presidency, Parliament, the Supreme Court, the High Council of State and the Constitutional Council.
Les tapis « hanib » sont tissés à la mai: 'Hanib' rugs are hand-woven by Moorish women, with ancestral geometric patterns.
Les taux de scolarisation et d'achèvemen: Enrolment and completion rates are significantly lower for girls, especially beyond primary school.

Les tribus berbères (Imazighen) se séden: The Berber tribes (Imazighen) settle in the oases and establish trade routes across the Sahara. Les zones rurales et nomades font face à: Rural and nomadic areas face a glaring shortage of school infrastructure and qualified teachers.

Malgré l'aridité extrême du Sahara, la M: Despite the extreme aridity of the Sahara, Mauritania shelters a surprising flora. Acacias, tamarisks and oasis date palms form screens of greenery in the heart of the desert. In the south, along the Senegal River, denser vegetation develops: baobabs, kapok trees and mango trees create a green border that contrasts with the sandy immensity. Traditional medicinal plants, such as guelguet and moringa, play an essential role in the local pharmacopoeia.
